lines: What sort of people live about here?

turns.speaker: cheshire_cat
lines: In that direction,
lives a Hatter: and in that direction,
lives a March Hare. Visit either you like: they're both mad.

turns.speaker: alice
lines: But I don't want to go among mad people,

turns.speaker: cheshire_cat
lines: Oh, you can't help that,
we're all mad here. I'm mad. You're mad.

turns.speaker: alice
lines: How do you know I'm mad?

turns.speaker: cheshire_cat
lines: You must be,
or you wouldn't have come here.

turns.speaker: alice
lines: And how do you know that you're mad?

turns.speaker: cheshire_cat
lines: To begin with,
a dog's not mad. You grant that?

turns.speaker: alice
lines: I suppose so,

turns.speaker: cheshire_cat
lines: Well, then,
you see, a dog growls when it's angry, and wags its tail when it's pleased. Now I growl when I'm pleased, and wag my tail when I'm angry. Therefore I'm mad.

turns.speaker: alice
lines: I call it purring, not growling,

turns.speaker: cheshire_cat
lines: Call it what you like,
Do you play croquet with the Queen to-day?

turns.speaker: alice
lines: I should like it very much,
but I haven't been invited yet.

turns.speaker: cheshire_cat
lines: You'll see me there,
By-the-bye, what became of the baby?
I'd nearly forgotten to ask.

turns.speaker: alice
lines: It turned into a pig,

turns.speaker: cheshire_cat
lines: I thought it would,

turns.speaker: alice
lines: I've seen hatters before;
the March Hare will be much the most interesting, and perhaps as this is May it won't be raving mad—at least not so mad as it was in March.

turns.speaker: cheshire_cat
lines: Did you say pig, or fig?

turns.speaker: alice
lines: I said pig,
and I wish you wouldn't keep appearing and vanishing so suddenly: you make one quite giddy.

turns.speaker: cheshire_cat
lines: All right,

turns.speaker: alice
lines: Suppose it should be raving mad after all!
I almost wish I'd gone to see the Hatter instead!
